title: Phase 1B delivered-client static analysis
method: Read saved byte sequences and inspect static logic only. No application JavaScript execution, navigation, network fetch, credentials, action call or original-source mutation.
offset_convention: Zero-based raw byte offsets; end is exclusive. Snippets are exact contiguous UTF-8 slices. HTTP ledger evidence also identifies a zero-based JSON array pointer.

coverage.snapshot: Initial nine plus four later successful exact observed assets; earlier CallSheetUpload reference GET returned 404

assets.classification: Framework: React DOM shared exports, Flight client codec and action dispatcher.
Library: core-js global polyfills and feature tests.
Gentry component: DateRangePicker and enclosing-form submission.
Mixed: Next Link/URL helpers; Gentry navigation and theme modules.
Mixed: Next Link/URL helpers; additional Gentry navigation/theme variant.
Framework: React, Next routing/error helpers and contexts.
Mixed: server-reference helper exports; CallSheetUpload client state and action identity.
Framework: Next App Router bootstrap and React DOM renderer.
Framework: Next router queue/cache/navigation and action protocol.
Framework: Next default global error page and styles.

findings.title: Shared application navigation
findings.conclusion: Module 56850 exports Icon, Logo, SideNav and TabNav. Logo renders a link to / labeled Gentry Ops. SideNav and TabNav render items supplied through props. Selected navigation uses exact match or the longest matching non-root path prefix.
findings.limits: No actual navigation item list is embedded here. A link string proves client-code intent, not route availability or authorization. Icon names, including users, are drawing options, not role rules.

findings.title: Navigation overflow behavior
findings.conclusion: TabNav scrolls its selected aria-current=page item into view when the selected path changes.
findings.limits: This display behavior neither inspects record state nor enforces access.

findings.title: Theme preference
findings.conclusion: ThemeToggle takes initialDark and toggles the document dark class on click. It writes theme=dark or light with path=/, max-age=31536000 and samesite=lax, then updates local state.
findings.limits: This is a presentation cookie. It does not identify a login cookie, token, session backend or permission implementation. No theme click was performed by this worker.

findings.title: Turbopack bootstrap
findings.conclusion: The bootstrap registers delivered chunks and runtime module 94553. The chunk-loader base path defaults to /_next/.
findings.limits: A bundle manifest is not a backend inventory. Unseen chunks may carry page components. This worker fetched no chunk referenced only in code strings.

findings.title: Delivered Next.js version declaration
findings.conclusion: The bootstrap assigns window.next={version:"16.3.5",appDir:!0}. This identifies the version declaration shipped in these bytes and App Router mode.
findings.limits: This is not package.json, a lockfile, backend source, or independent proof of every server dependency.

findings.title: Delivered React version declarations
findings.conclusion: React and React DOM declare 19.3.0-canary-cbb046ab-20260731. React DOM also checks the React version against that literal.
findings.limits: These are delivered runtime declarations, not a recommendation for a replacement system.

findings.title: Polyfill library
findings.conclusion: The polyfill chunk records core-js version 3.38.1 in global mode with license/source URLs.
findings.limits: Polyfill URLs and URL-parser test values are library content, not Gentry integrations or production endpoints.

findings.title: Flight transport headers
findings.conclusion: The framework declares rsc, next-action, next-router-state-tree, next-router-prefetch, next-router-segment-prefetch, next-hmr-refresh, next-url and text/x-component constants. It also declares _rsc, action-not-found and action-revalidated markers.
findings.limits: These define transport implementation available in this build. Actual authenticated requests and response values require separate browser/network observations.

findings.title: Initial Flight hydration
findings.conclusion: The bootstrap consumes self.__next_f into a ReadableStream. Tag 0 initializes a queue, 1 carries encoded text, 2 sets form state, and 3 decodes base64 binary bytes. It then calls createFromReadableStream, or createFromFetch for client-resume/test paths.
findings.limits: Protocol support exposes no domain status transition or per-user access rule. No Flight payload was inspected within this delegated input scope.

findings.title: Flight navigation requests
findings.conclusion: Navigation fetch prepares RSC and router-state headers, optionally next-url, and requests with credentials:same-origin. Non-Flight, failed, bodyless or mismatched-build responses fall back to browser navigation.
findings.limits: The generic credentials option does not prove cookie names, expiry, session backend or which Gentry routes were requested.

findings.title: Server-action dispatch
findings.conclusion: callServer returns a Promise and dispatches ACTION_SERVER_ACTION with actionId, actionArgs, resolve and reject inside startTransition.
findings.limits: Identity and arguments are supplied dynamically. This dispatcher names no Gentry business function.

findings.title: Server references and bound arguments
findings.conclusion: The React client provides createServerReference, which wraps an identifier and callback. It resolves streamed references through id and bound fields, concatenating bound arguments before calling the server callback.
findings.limits: The initial nine assets expose the generic reference machinery. A later retained app-specific chunk supplies uploadCallSheet with a literal action ID (APP10). Rendered forms/Flight may carry other identities separately.

findings.title: Server-action HTTP protocol
findings.conclusion: The reducer encodes action arguments with encodeReply, sends a POST to the current canonical URL, and places the dynamic ID in next-action. Accept is text/x-component, router state is encoded, and optional deployment/next-url fields are added.
findings.limits: This does not identify a Gentry-specific /api action route or establish server validation, authorization, side effects, idempotency or successful execution. No action was called.

findings.title: Server-action response handling
findings.conclusion: The reducer checks x-nextjs-action-not-found, parses x-action-redirect with push/replace, parses x-action-revalidated and decodes a Flight response. It rejects an unexpected non-Flight response when no redirect was supplied.
findings.limits: These generic outcomes cannot establish operation-specific Gentry success, retry or audit rules.

findings.title: Server-reference identifier format
findings.conclusion: The helper expects length 42. The first hex byte encodes use-cache versus server-action, six used-argument bits and a rest-arguments bit. omitUnusedArgs builds the outgoing argument list.
findings.limits: One literal 42-character hexadecimal identity appears in the 13 retained assets: uploadCallSheet (APP10). The format decoder does not establish handler semantics or access policy.

findings.title: Router refresh implementation
findings.conclusion: Public app-router refresh dispatches ACTION_REFRESH inside startTransition. The queue may request refresh after a discarded server action revalidated data. Generic error retry also calls context refresh before resetting error state.
findings.limits: No recurring Gentry data-refresh cadence is established by the 13 retained assets. PrintButton has a one-shot print timeout (APP08). Route refresh and server-side integration synchronization remain different questions; server jobs are not ruled out.

findings.title: HTTP fallback display does not establish RBAC
findings.conclusion: HTTPAccessFallbackBoundary displays supplied notFound/forbidden/unauthorized components when corresponding framework error statuses are thrown. React role matches concern ARIA/DOM attributes.
findings.limits: Fallback display does not prove a Gentry authorization check or role matrix. No app-specific role predicate was identified in retained component functions; upstream prop selection and server authorization remain unknown.

findings.title: Domain-like strings with unrelated framework meaning
findings.conclusion: WhatsApp appears in a bot-user-agent regex. cleanup names an LRU/cache export and call. Neither is Gentry WhatsApp integration or order-cleanup workflow evidence.
findings.limits: Meta matches concern metadata/polyfills; users is an icon key. Explicit Shopify/Bosta/Whapi connector configuration or request code was not identified in retained assets; server integrations remain outside this evidence.

findings.title: Server behavior outside retained client coverage
findings.conclusion: The 13 retained assets confirm navigation, date selection, browser printing, CallSheetUpload client state/identity and shared framework transport. They do not establish server import rules, role enforcement, integration jobs or recurring refresh cadence.
findings.limits: The earlier referenced CallSheetUpload chunk returned 404; a freshly observed exact chunk later returned 200. The discrepancy cause is unresolved. More rendered-form/Flight or server evidence may close gaps. String discovery never access-verifies a route.

findings.title: Additional shared-navigation asset variant
findings.conclusion: The newly retained 1986ffcy11vyr.js again exports module 56850 Icon/Logo/SideNav/TabNav and module 94013 ThemeToggle. It includes a check drawing in the icon map, alongside existing icons. SideNav receives items and direction; TabNav receives items. Both map supplied items to links and select by pathname; neither filters them by a role/permission prop or predicate in these functions.
findings.limits: The variant does not supply a route or label list. An upstream server may select props before rendering; this client module cannot establish that server policy. A check icon establishes a drawing option, not a named workflow, feature flag or permission. Different hashed assets with the same module IDs do not establish deployment chronology.

findings.title: DateRangePicker props and preset submission
findings.conclusion: Module 16340 exports DateRangePicker with period, from, to, today, min, presets, weeks and note props. It keeps period and To in component state. Choosing a preset or nonempty week sets local period, writes that value immediately to its hidden period input, disables date inputs within the component, and calls requestSubmit on the closest enclosing form.
findings.limits: The component does not declare the enclosing form method or action. GET filtering requires separately observed rendered-form evidence. No fetch, server-action identity, integration or data mutation is defined in this component. Disabling date controls excludes them from normal form submission; backend interpretation of the remaining period is not exposed.

findings.title: Custom dates and native input limits
findings.conclusion: From is a date input named from with defaultValue from, min=min and max=today. To is named to with controlled state, the same bounds, and onChange updating To and selecting custom. Editing From also selects custom. The till today button appears when To differs from today and sets To=today plus period=custom without calling requestSubmit.
findings.limits: These are client input attributes and state updates. No from<=to comparison, date arithmetic, timezone conversion, invalid-date parser or server validation is shown. Today and min arrive as props, so their computation and values cannot be inferred. From uses defaultValue; both inputs should not be described as controlled.

findings.title: Week selection and preset display logic
findings.conclusion: The week select displays period when it starts with w, otherwise an empty value; it submits only a nonempty selection. Week options and preset buttons come from supplied arrays. A preset is highlighted when its key equals period, or when key=last-week and period is empty. Optional note is rendered as text.
findings.limits: The startsWith("w") convention does not establish week definitions, date boundaries, inclusivity or server presets. The selected last-week appearance for empty period is display logic, not proof of a backend default. No feature flag or role-dependent option filtering appears.

findings.title: PrintButton one-shot timer and manual printing
findings.conclusion: Module 44026 exports PrintButton with auto defaulting false. Its effect returns immediately unless auto is true; when true it schedules window.print after 400 ms and clears that timer on effect cleanup. The Save as PDF button calls window.print immediately on click.
findings.limits: This is browser print UI, not a server PDF-generation endpoint. Browser/user controls output destination and saving. auto is a presentation prop, not evidence of a business feature flag or permission. The 400 ms timeout is a one-shot print delay, not recurring refresh or an integration job. This worker triggered no print or download.

findings.title: Local persistence and refresh coverage limits
findings.conclusion: The retained app-specific navigation, DateRangePicker, PrintButton and CallSheetUpload functions contain no localStorage/sessionStorage, draft save/restore, recurring setInterval, role predicate or client integration request. DateRangePicker keeps current selections in React state; ThemeToggle writes a presentation cookie; PrintButton uses a one-shot timeout; CallSheetUpload uses React action state.
findings.limits: This is limited to retained client functions. It does not establish absent server jobs, absent application-wide autosave, absent scheduled integrations or no refresh elsewhere. CallSheetUpload exposes no explicit local-draft implementation; its server handler and any other component remain outside this analysis.

findings.title: CallSheetUpload server-reference identity
findings.conclusion: The newly retained 1t_el1w5uiobt.js module 4773 exports CallSheetUpload. It creates a server reference with the literal identity 603a2551faaf2a276b438c3b70de362ad8e990c011 and the symbol uploadCallSheet, using the framework callServer/findSourceMapURL helpers. The generic first-byte decoder (FW12) reads 0x60 as server-action, used argument positions 0 and 1, and no rest-arguments bit.
findings.limits: This is a public delivered-client action identity and symbol, not server-handler source or an authorization credential. Its name is not proof of row matching, duplicate detection, import limits, transactions or side effects. No action was invoked, file selected or production row imported. The association is scoped to these observed bytes; future builds may change the identity.

findings.title: Call importer state and response feedback
findings.conclusion: CallSheetUpload calls useActionState on that reference with an empty initial object. Its returned action function is assigned to the form. The pending value disables the Import button and changes its label from Import calls to Importing. Truthy state.error renders as error text. Truthy state.result renders added, alreadyThere, noCallStatus and unmatched.length, with unmatched examples limited to the first 15 entries.
findings.limits: The client expects this result shape; no actual import response was observed. alreadyThere suggests server-reported duplicate handling but does not prove its key or algorithm. noCallStatus is feedback labeled rows without a call status skipped, not a client validation implementation. The list entries are returned strings; none were fetched or retained in this review. No explicit reset, success-triggered router.refresh or file-input disable appears in the component.

findings.title: Call importer file chooser and validation boundary
findings.conclusion: The importer file input is named file and has accept=".csv,text/csv". Its component has no required attribute, size limit, explicit client CSV parser, content/schema checks or row validation. The form is bound to the server-action function; the surrounding shared framework handles action transport.
findings.limits: accept is a chooser hint rather than evidence of server validation. Importing safely and determining required columns, matching rules, duplicate keys and write consequences requires server source or a separately approved test. A component-level lack of role props does not prove the server action lacks permission enforcement. Local draft persistence is not exposed by this component.

findings.title: Time-scoped referenced CallSheetUpload asset discrepancy
findings.conclusion: The ledger records exact 1kudf3dkhdpbd.js GET at 2026-10-13T16:58:51.804164+00:00 with 404, text/plain content type, a 9-byte response and body_retained=false. The parent investigation reports this was a Calls Flight reference for module 4773 CallSheetUpload. A fresh Calls navigation later reported module 4773 in 1t_el1w5uiobt.js; its exact GET at 2026-10-13T17:00:35.974352+00:00 returned 200 and the code was retained/analyzed.
findings.limits: The corrected HTTP ledger classifies the earlier 404 response as error body; discarded. It remains a failed asset attempt, with no response body retained. Its cause remains unresolved. No deployment, stale cache or transient failure explanation is established. Calls navigation/Flight association is supplied parent context; this worker inspected only the saved JS and ledger. No guessed alternative was fetched.
findings.classification: Verified fact (recorded HTTP responses); Flight associations supplied by parent investigation
